questions.prompt: Which term describes the written analysis of a play's sources, context, structure, and meaning before rehearsal?
options: Dramaturgy
Ticketing
Wardrobe storage
Camera charging
questions.correctAnswer: Dramaturgy
questions.explanation: Dramaturgy supports informed theatre-making by studying the world, form, themes, and performance possibilities of a script.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify dramaturgy as a tool for informed performance creation.

questions.prompt: What is subtext in acting?
options: The unspoken meaning beneath a character's words
The printed title of a script only
A list of props in a storeroom
The price written on a ticket
questions.correctAnswer: The unspoken meaning beneath a character's words
questions.explanation: Subtext helps actors communicate hidden feelings, motives, and tensions beyond the literal dialogue.
questions.learningOutcome: Define subtext as part of character interpretation.

questions.prompt: Which word names the central character's journey of change across a play or film?
options: Character arc
Lighting grid
Box office
Call sheet
questions.correctAnswer: Character arc
questions.explanation: A character arc traces how a character's choices, beliefs, or relationships develop through the story.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify character arc in dramatic writing.

questions.prompt: Which document lists the scenes to be filmed each day, locations, cast, crew, and call times?
options: Call sheet
Monologue
Plot twist
Costume swatch
questions.correctAnswer: Call sheet
questions.explanation: A call sheet organises a filming day by communicating practical details to the production team.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify key documents used in film production planning.

questions.prompt: What is mise-en-scene in film analysis?
options: The arrangement of visual elements within a shot
The sound level of applause only
A list of camera brands
The number of tickets sold
questions.correctAnswer: The arrangement of visual elements within a shot
questions.explanation: Mise-en-scene includes setting, costume, lighting, props, actor placement, and visual composition.
questions.learningOutcome: Define mise-en-scene as a film-language concept.

questions.prompt: Which term refers to a short uninterrupted piece of acting performed by one actor?
options: Monologue
Storyboard
Montage
Cue sheet
questions.correctAnswer: Monologue
questions.explanation: A monologue gives one performer an extended speech that reveals thought, emotion, or dramatic action.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise monologue as a form of dramatic performance.

questions.prompt: Which role coordinates lighting, sound, scene changes, entrances, and cues during a live performance?
options: Stage manager
Public spectator
Film critic
Poster printer
questions.correctAnswer: Stage manager
questions.explanation: The stage manager keeps the live performance running in order by coordinating cues and production communication.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the responsibilities of a stage manager.

questions.prompt: What is a shot list in film production?
options: A planned list of shots needed for a scene or project
A theatre seating arrangement
A costume washing schedule
A record of audience applause
questions.correctAnswer: A planned list of shots needed for a scene or project
questions.explanation: A shot list helps the director and camera team capture the visual material needed for editing.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify a shot list as a film planning tool.

questions.prompt: Which term means adapting a story, poem, or oral narrative into a play or film?
options: Dramatisation
Ticket reservation
Light cleaning
Curtain folding
questions.correctAnswer: Dramatisation
questions.explanation: Dramatisation transforms source material into performable action, dialogue, scenes, and images.
questions.learningOutcome: Define dramatisation in theatre and film creation.

questions.prompt: Which rehearsal focuses on integrating lighting, sound, props, set changes, and performance timing?
options: Technical rehearsal
Silent reading
Ticket audit
Costume shopping
questions.correctAnswer: Technical rehearsal
questions.explanation: A technical rehearsal tests how performers and technical elements work together before presentation.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise the purpose of technical rehearsal.

questions.prompt: Which term describes permission from a performer or participant to be filmed or recorded?
options: Consent
Projection
Blocking
Foreshadowing
questions.correctAnswer: Consent
questions.explanation: Consent is an ethical and practical requirement when recording people for performance or film work.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify consent as an ethical requirement in recording performance.

questions.prompt: Which film editing term describes a series of short shots joined to show time passing or ideas developing?
options: Montage
Soliloquy
Apron stage
Costume fitting
questions.correctAnswer: Montage
questions.explanation: A montage compresses events or builds meaning through selected images placed in sequence.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify montage as a film editing technique.

questions.prompt: Which term means the planned path a performer follows across the stage?
options: Movement pathway
Copyright notice
Camera sensor
Budget line
questions.correctAnswer: Movement pathway
questions.explanation: Movement pathways organise stage action so performers move safely and meaningfully through the space.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify movement pathways in stage blocking.

questions.prompt: What is a production concept?
options: The guiding artistic idea that unifies performance choices
The total number of seats in a hall
A random list of actor names
The brand of the editing laptop
questions.correctAnswer: The guiding artistic idea that unifies performance choices
questions.explanation: A production concept gives direction to acting, design, staging, sound, and audience communication.
questions.learningOutcome: Define production concept in theatre and film.

questions.prompt: Which term describes income earned from creative activities such as performances, filming, teaching, or production services?
options: Creative enterprise
Stage direction
Close-up
Scene partner
questions.correctAnswer: Creative enterprise
questions.explanation: Creative enterprise links artistic skill with responsible income generation and sustainable production practice.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise creative enterprise in Performing Arts careers.

questions.prompt: Why should a Grade 11 actor analyse a character's objective before rehearsing a scene?
options: It clarifies what the character wants and guides performance choices
It removes the need to listen to other actors
It makes every line sound the same
It replaces the director's rehearsal plan
questions.correctAnswer: It clarifies what the character wants and guides performance choices
questions.explanation: An objective gives the actor a clear intention that shapes voice, movement, pace, and interaction.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how objectives guide character performance.

questions.prompt: Why is table work useful at the start of rehearsing a scripted scene?
options: It helps the cast discuss meaning, relationships, context, and questions before staging
It allows performers to avoid rehearsing movement forever
It makes the script unnecessary
It guarantees ticket sales before auditions
questions.correctAnswer: It helps the cast discuss meaning, relationships, context, and questions before staging
questions.explanation: Table work builds shared understanding so later rehearsal decisions are more informed.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of table work in rehearsal.

questions.prompt: How does foreshadowing strengthen a dramatic story?
options: It plants clues that prepare later events without revealing everything
It removes all suspense from the performance
It forces every scene to end happily
It makes characters ignore consequences
questions.correctAnswer: It plants clues that prepare later events without revealing everything
questions.explanation: Foreshadowing creates anticipation and makes later events feel connected to earlier action.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how foreshadowing supports dramatic structure.

questions.prompt: Why should a film crew record room tone at a location?
options: To help smooth sound edits by capturing the natural background sound
To replace all dialogue with silence
To measure the size of the classroom
To decide costume colours
questions.correctAnswer: To help smooth sound edits by capturing the natural background sound
questions.explanation: Room tone provides consistent background audio that can make edited dialogue sound continuous.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the use of room tone in film sound editing.

questions.prompt: Why is a release form useful when filming interviews for a school documentary?
options: It records permission and clarifies how the footage may be used
It automatically improves camera focus
It replaces respectful questioning
It removes the need to credit sources
questions.correctAnswer: It records permission and clarifies how the footage may be used
questions.explanation: Release forms protect participants and producers by documenting consent and intended use of recordings.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why consent records matter in documentary work.

questions.prompt: Why does a director use contrast in stage pictures?
options: To create visual interest and clarify relationships, focus, or tension
To make all performers stand in one line permanently
To hide the main action from the audience
To remove design from the production
questions.correctAnswer: To create visual interest and clarify relationships, focus, or tension
questions.explanation: Contrasting levels, distance, direction, and grouping can communicate meaning before any dialogue is spoken.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how contrast supports stage composition.

questions.prompt: Why should learners credit a community storyteller when adapting an oral narrative?
options: It respects authorship, source knowledge, and cultural ownership
It makes the performance less ethical
It prevents any creative interpretation
It hides the origin of the material
questions.correctAnswer: It respects authorship, source knowledge, and cultural ownership
questions.explanation: Attribution recognises the people and communities whose knowledge contributes to the performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain ethical attribution when adapting community-sourced material.

questions.prompt: How does a reaction shot support film storytelling?
options: It shows how a character responds emotionally or mentally to an event
It proves that no editing is needed
It hides the actor's expression
It replaces the scene's conflict with titles
questions.correctAnswer: It shows how a character responds emotionally or mentally to an event
questions.explanation: Reaction shots help viewers read relationships, consequences, and emotional shifts in a scene.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how reaction shots communicate character response.

questions.prompt: Why should stage props be checked before every performance?
options: To ensure they are safe, present, functional, and placed correctly
To make the script longer
To increase audience noise
To avoid rehearsing with actors
questions.correctAnswer: To ensure they are safe, present, functional, and placed correctly
questions.explanation: Prop checks prevent delays, unsafe handling, and broken action during live performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of prop checks in production readiness.

questions.prompt: What makes an audition notice effective for a school theatre or film project?
options: It gives roles, requirements, date, time, venue, preparation task, and contact details
It only says that something may happen soon
It hides the venue until after auditions
It asks learners to guess every requirement
questions.correctAnswer: It gives roles, requirements, date, time, venue, preparation task, and contact details
questions.explanation: Clear audition information helps interested performers prepare and attend fairly.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain clear communication in audition planning.

questions.prompt: Why is continuity especially important when filming one conversation from different angles?
options: It keeps action, eyelines, props, and costume consistent across shots
It requires every actor to wear the same costume forever
It removes the need for editing decisions
It prevents the camera from changing position
questions.correctAnswer: It keeps action, eyelines, props, and costume consistent across shots
questions.explanation: Continuity helps viewers experience separate shots as one believable scene.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain continuity needs in multi-shot filming.

questions.prompt: Why should feedback after a rehearsal name specific evidence from the performance?
options: It makes the feedback clearer, fairer, and easier to act on
It guarantees that no performer will improve
It avoids discussing the actual scene
It turns feedback into a popularity vote
questions.correctAnswer: It makes the feedback clearer, fairer, and easier to act on
questions.explanation: Evidence-based feedback links comments to observable choices such as voice, timing, movement, or focus.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain qualities of useful performance feedback.

questions.prompt: Why might a theatre designer choose symbolic set pieces instead of a fully realistic set?
options: To suggest meaning economically while supporting movement and scene changes
To make the audience unable to see performers
To remove all connection to the story
To avoid any design thinking
questions.correctAnswer: To suggest meaning economically while supporting movement and scene changes
questions.explanation: Symbolic design can communicate place, mood, and theme without needing many detailed objects.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of symbolic set design.

questions.prompt: How can a soundscape support a stage performance?
options: By creating atmosphere, location, rhythm, or emotional tension through sound
By replacing every actor on stage
By making movement unsafe
By hiding all spoken words all the time
questions.correctAnswer: By creating atmosphere, location, rhythm, or emotional tension through sound
questions.explanation: A soundscape uses selected sound to shape the audience's sense of place, mood, and action.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the function of soundscape in theatre.

questions.prompt: Why should performers vary tempo in a dramatic scene?
options: To shape tension, emphasis, mood, and changes in thought
To make every scene the same speed
To make the script shorter automatically
To remove emotional meaning from lines
questions.correctAnswer: To shape tension, emphasis, mood, and changes in thought
questions.explanation: Tempo affects how the audience experiences urgency, silence, hesitation, conflict, and release.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how tempo affects dramatic performance.

questions.prompt: Why is audience analysis useful before creating a performance on a social issue?
options: It helps the group choose tone, examples, language, and form that suit viewers
It means the group should flatter every viewer
It removes the need for a clear message
It prevents learners from researching the issue
questions.correctAnswer: It helps the group choose tone, examples, language, and form that suit viewers
questions.explanation: Knowing the intended audience supports relevant, respectful, and effective communication.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how audience analysis informs performance planning.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a pitch for a short film idea?
options: To communicate the story, audience, style, resources, and value of the project clearly
To read every line of dialogue from the script
To hide the production plan from collaborators
To replace filming with a poster
questions.correctAnswer: To communicate the story, audience, style, resources, and value of the project clearly
questions.explanation: A pitch helps others understand and support a film before full production begins.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of pitching a theatre or film project.

questions.prompt: Why should a screenplay use scene headings?
options: To show location and time so the production team can plan scenes
To make actors speak louder
To describe audience seating only
To remove conflict from the story
questions.correctAnswer: To show location and time so the production team can plan scenes
questions.explanation: Scene headings identify where and when a scene happens, supporting scheduling, filming, and reading clarity.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of scene headings in screenwriting.

questions.prompt: Why is ensemble listening important during improvised performance?
options: It lets performers accept offers, build action, and avoid blocking partners' ideas
It allows one performer to ignore everyone else
It makes the audience decide the plot alone
It prevents any character relationship from forming
questions.correctAnswer: It lets performers accept offers, build action, and avoid blocking partners' ideas
questions.explanation: Strong improvisation depends on attentive response so shared action can develop coherently.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain listening as a foundation of ensemble improvisation.

questions.prompt: How does costume continuity support a film scene shot over several hours?
options: It prevents accidental changes that would distract viewers between shots
It makes every film scene historically accurate
It removes the need for actors to rehearse
It means costumes cannot express character
questions.correctAnswer: It prevents accidental changes that would distract viewers between shots
questions.explanation: Continuity records help costumes, hair, and props remain consistent when shots are filmed out of order.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of costume continuity in film.

questions.prompt: Why is risk assessment needed before staging a fight scene?
options: To plan safe movement, supervision, spacing, rehearsal, and alternatives
To make the fight look uncontrolled
To encourage performers to surprise each other
To remove all teacher guidance
questions.correctAnswer: To plan safe movement, supervision, spacing, rehearsal, and alternatives
questions.explanation: Choreographed conflict must protect performers while still communicating dramatic tension.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain safety planning for staged conflict.

questions.prompt: Why should copyrighted music be checked before using it in a public film screening?
options: Creators' rights and permission conditions must be respected
Any song becomes free if learners like it
Crediting a source removes every legal concern
Copyright applies only to printed books
questions.correctAnswer: Creators' rights and permission conditions must be respected
questions.explanation: Responsible production checks ownership, licensing, and permitted use before sharing creative work publicly.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain copyright responsibilities in performance and film production.

questions.prompt: How does a storyboard help a film director communicate with the camera team?
options: It shows planned images, framing, action, and order before filming
It replaces all rehearsal with costume labels
It counts ticket sales after the screening
It records only the actors' phone numbers
questions.correctAnswer: It shows planned images, framing, action, and order before filming
questions.explanation: Storyboards turn script ideas into visual plans that guide filming and collaboration.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how storyboards support visual planning.

questions.prompt: Why does a director give notes after a rehearsal run?
options: To refine performance choices while keeping the production concept clear
To punish actors for trying new ideas
To cancel every earlier decision automatically
To avoid watching the scene carefully
questions.correctAnswer: To refine performance choices while keeping the production concept clear
questions.explanation: Director's notes guide improvement in timing, interpretation, focus, movement, and clarity.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of director's notes in rehearsal improvement.

questions.prompt: Why is a balanced production budget important for a school performance?
options: It aligns available resources with artistic, technical, safety, and publicity needs
It proves that expensive design is always best
It removes the need for receipts or records
It lets one area spend everything without planning
questions.correctAnswer: It aligns available resources with artistic, technical, safety, and publicity needs
questions.explanation: Budgeting helps the team prioritise essential costs and avoid waste or shortages.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the value of balanced budgeting in production.

questions.prompt: A scene shows two friends arguing, but both actors face away from each other throughout. Which first adjustment best clarifies relationship and conflict?
options: Use blocking that lets them face, avoid, and shift distance according to changing tension
Ask both actors to speak faster without listening
Remove all movement and turn off the lights
Add unrelated background dancers
questions.correctAnswer: Use blocking that lets them face, avoid, and shift distance according to changing tension
questions.explanation: Blocking should make relationship changes visible through distance, direction, levels, and focus.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply blocking choices to clarify dramatic relationships.

questions.prompt: A learner is adapting a folktale for a five-minute film. Which step should come first?
options: Identify the core conflict, moral lesson, key characters, and permission needs
Choose expensive effects before understanding the story
Film random scenes and invent the plot later
Remove the original source from all planning
questions.correctAnswer: Identify the core conflict, moral lesson, key characters, and permission needs
questions.explanation: Adaptation begins by understanding what must be preserved and what can be transformed responsibly.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply responsible steps when adapting oral narratives for screen.

questions.prompt: A short film opens with a learner staring at muddy shoes before entering a clean classroom. What does the opening shot most likely establish?
options: A visual clue that may connect character, setting, and coming conflict
A guarantee that no story will follow
An instruction to ignore props
A scene with no possible meaning
questions.correctAnswer: A visual clue that may connect character, setting, and coming conflict
questions.explanation: Opening visual details can introduce character situation, mood, and questions for viewers.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply visual clues to infer story meaning.

questions.prompt: A group wants to show a crowded bus stage scene with only four actors. Which staging choice is most effective?
options: Use sound cues, repeated movement, close spacing, and mime to suggest crowding
Cancel the scene because four actors cannot suggest a crowd
Ask one actor to explain the entire setting without action
Fill the stage with unsafe furniture
questions.correctAnswer: Use sound cues, repeated movement, close spacing, and mime to suggest crowding
questions.explanation: Theatre can suggest a larger world through ensemble movement, sound, spacing, and symbolic action.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply economical staging techniques to suggest environment.

questions.prompt: A performer keeps smiling while delivering lines about disappointment. Which acting adjustment would best support believable characterisation?
options: Align facial expression, vocal tone, gesture, and objective with the character's emotional state
Speak the lines louder while keeping the same expression
Ignore the character's situation and focus only on costume
Let another actor explain the emotion to the audience
questions.correctAnswer: Align facial expression, vocal tone, gesture, and objective with the character's emotional state
questions.explanation: Believable acting requires coordinated physical and vocal choices that fit the dramatic moment.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply expressive choices to create believable characterisation.

questions.prompt: A documentary team interviews a market vendor about recycling. Which question is most suitable for gaining useful personal detail?
options: How has recycling changed your daily work at the market?
Do you like recycling, yes or no only?
What is the answer the teacher wants?
Can you repeat the poster slogan exactly?
questions.correctAnswer: How has recycling changed your daily work at the market?
questions.explanation: Open questions invite specific experience, evidence, and voice, which are useful in documentary storytelling.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply open-ended questioning in documentary production.

questions.prompt: A production team has a small budget for costumes. Which choice best supports character and sustainability?
options: Select simple adaptable costume pieces that signal role, status, or period clearly
Buy many expensive outfits before casting roles
Use identical costumes for all characters regardless of meaning
Ignore costume safety and comfort
questions.correctAnswer: Select simple adaptable costume pieces that signal role, status, or period clearly
questions.explanation: Effective costume design can be economical while still communicating character and context.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply resource-aware costume design choices.

questions.prompt: A director wants to show a character becoming isolated during a scene. Which blocking choice best communicates this?
options: Gradually increase the physical distance between the character and the group
Keep every performer in a tight circle without change
Make all actors face the same direction throughout
Move the isolated character only after the scene ends
questions.correctAnswer: Gradually increase the physical distance between the character and the group
questions.explanation: Changing spatial relationships can make emotional separation visible to the audience.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply space to communicate character relationships.

questions.prompt: A learner writes a screenplay scene with no conflict, decision, or change. Which revision would most improve it?
options: Give a character a clear goal, obstacle, choice, and consequence
Add more font styles to the page
Remove all dialogue and action
Make the location heading longer only
questions.correctAnswer: Give a character a clear goal, obstacle, choice, and consequence
questions.explanation: A dramatic scene usually needs a want, resistance, choice, and result to move the story forward.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply dramatic structure to improve scene writing.

questions.prompt: A film crew has noisy wind during an outdoor dialogue scene. What is the best practical response?
options: Move to a sheltered spot, protect the microphone, and monitor the sound before filming
Record anyway and hope the editor removes every problem
Ask actors to mime all dialogue without planning
Point the microphone away from the speakers
questions.correctAnswer: Move to a sheltered spot, protect the microphone, and monitor the sound before filming
questions.explanation: Good sound recording requires controlling noise sources and checking audio quality during production.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply practical sound-recording choices on location.

questions.prompt: A group is creating a theatre piece about cyberbullying for younger learners. Which approach best fits the audience?
options: Use clear characters, age-appropriate language, realistic consequences, and a hopeful action step
Use complex adult legal language throughout
Make the issue funny by mocking victims
Avoid showing any decision or consequence
questions.correctAnswer: Use clear characters, age-appropriate language, realistic consequences, and a hopeful action step
questions.explanation: Audience-appropriate theatre communicates serious issues clearly and responsibly without harm or confusion.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply audience-aware choices when dramatising contemporary issues.

questions.prompt: A stage manager notices two cue numbers are repeated in the prompt copy. What should happen before the next rehearsal?
options: Renumber and confirm cues with the technical team to avoid confusion
Ignore the issue until opening night
Tell actors to guess the cues during performance
Delete all cue notes from the script
questions.correctAnswer: Renumber and confirm cues with the technical team to avoid confusion
questions.explanation: Clear cue documentation prevents missed or mistimed technical actions in performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply accurate documentation in stage management.

questions.prompt: A learner wants a shot that makes a character appear powerful. Which camera choice is most suitable?
options: A low-angle shot looking up at the character
A random shot of the ceiling fan
A blurred shot of the actor's shoes only
A cutaway to unrelated trees
questions.correctAnswer: A low-angle shot looking up at the character
questions.explanation: Low-angle framing can make a character appear dominant, imposing, or significant.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply camera angle choices to communicate character power.

questions.prompt: A scene requires a moment of shock after unexpected news. Which performance choice best supports the beat?
options: Use a brief pause, changed focus, and altered breath before the next line
Rush immediately into the next line with no change
Add unrelated dance steps during the news
Turn the moment into casual laughter without reason
questions.correctAnswer: Use a brief pause, changed focus, and altered breath before the next line
questions.explanation: A beat change lets the audience perceive new information affecting a character's thought and action.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply beat changes to communicate character response.

questions.prompt: A group is adapting a news report into a stage scene. Which choice makes the material dramatic instead of merely informational?
options: Create characters with opposing objectives affected by the event
Have actors read the full report without interaction
Project statistics and end without action
Remove every human consequence from the issue
questions.correctAnswer: Create characters with opposing objectives affected by the event
questions.explanation: Drama grows when information is embodied in character conflict, choices, and consequences.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply dramatic transformation to factual material.

questions.prompt: A film edit cuts from a learner reaching for a door handle to the learner entering the room. Which editing principle is being used?
options: Match on action
Direct address
Stage combat
Costume plot
questions.correctAnswer: Match on action
questions.explanation: Match on action connects continuous movement across two shots so the edit feels smooth.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply continuity editing concepts to shot transitions.

questions.prompt: A performance space has audience on three sides. What blocking priority should the director apply?
options: Keep important action visible from multiple angles without turning backs for too long
Face all actors permanently to one wall
Place key action behind the audience
Use large scenery that blocks two sides
questions.correctAnswer: Keep important action visible from multiple angles without turning backs for too long
questions.explanation: Thrust or three-sided staging needs flexible blocking that shares focus across audience areas.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply blocking choices for different performance spaces.

questions.prompt: A crew wants to publicise a school film screening responsibly. Which item should appear on the poster?
options: Title, date, time, venue, target audience, entry details, and contact information
Only a vague slogan with no screening details
Private phone numbers of all cast members
A copied film poster from another production
questions.correctAnswer: Title, date, time, venue, target audience, entry details, and contact information
questions.explanation: Responsible publicity gives useful information and avoids copying protected designs or exposing private details.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply clear and ethical publicity practices for performance events.

questions.prompt: A director asks actors to create a frozen image of a family disagreement. Which technique are they using?
options: Tableau
Voice-over
Jump cut
Budget forecast
questions.correctAnswer: Tableau
questions.explanation: A tableau is a still stage picture that communicates relationships, conflict, or theme through bodies in space.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply tableau to communicate dramatic meaning.

questions.prompt: A group wants to show time passing in a play without changing the whole set. Which design solution is strongest?
options: Use lighting shifts, sound cues, actor movement, and selected prop changes
Stop the performance for a long explanation
Replace the entire stage after every line
Ignore time changes and hope the audience guesses
questions.correctAnswer: Use lighting shifts, sound cues, actor movement, and selected prop changes
questions.explanation: Theatre can communicate time economically through coordinated performance and design cues.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply stagecraft to show changes in time and place.

questions.prompt: A learner is selecting music for an original film scene. Which choice is most responsible?
options: Use original, licensed, or permission-cleared music that supports the scene mood
Use any popular song without checking rights
Choose music that hides all important dialogue
Select music only because it is loud
questions.correctAnswer: Use original, licensed, or permission-cleared music that supports the scene mood
questions.explanation: Music choices should serve storytelling while respecting intellectual property and audience understanding.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply ethical and artistic criteria when selecting film music.

questions.prompt: A playwright wants the audience to understand a character's private fear without using narration. Which technique can help?
options: Show the fear through action, hesitation, gesture, or a revealing choice
Add a footnote in the programme only
Have another character read the author's notes
Remove the fear from the scene
questions.correctAnswer: Show the fear through action, hesitation, gesture, or a revealing choice
questions.explanation: Dramatic writing often reveals inner life through behaviour rather than explanation.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply dramatic action to reveal inner conflict.

questions.prompt: A group receives feedback that their final scene ends too suddenly. Which revision best improves resolution?
options: Add a consequence or final choice that answers the central conflict
Repeat the opening lines without change
End with unrelated singing only
Remove the conflict from earlier scenes
questions.correctAnswer: Add a consequence or final choice that answers the central conflict
questions.explanation: A resolution should show how the central conflict lands for characters and audience.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply revision strategies to strengthen dramatic endings.

questions.prompt: A film scene has dialogue in a noisy school compound. Which microphone placement best improves clarity?
options: Place the microphone close to the speakers while keeping it outside the frame
Keep the microphone far across the field
Cover the microphone completely with cloth
Point the microphone toward the loudest crowd
questions.correctAnswer: Place the microphone close to the speakers while keeping it outside the frame
questions.explanation: Close, well-aimed microphone placement improves dialogue clarity while preserving the image.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply microphone placement principles during filming.

questions.prompt: A school production includes a scene about grief. Which rehearsal practice is most appropriate?
options: Set respectful boundaries, discuss intention, rehearse safely, and support performers
Force performers to share personal trauma for realism
Mock the topic to make rehearsal easier
Avoid teacher supervision during emotional scenes
questions.correctAnswer: Set respectful boundaries, discuss intention, rehearse safely, and support performers
questions.explanation: Sensitive content requires care, consent, respectful process, and learner wellbeing.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply ethical rehearsal practices for sensitive material.

questions.prompt: A group wants to evaluate their rehearsal collaboration. Which evidence is most useful?
options: Attendance, preparation, listening, task completion, respect, and response to feedback
Only the loudest performer's opinion
Only costume colour preference
The number of jokes made during rehearsal
questions.correctAnswer: Attendance, preparation, listening, task completion, respect, and response to feedback
questions.explanation: Collaboration is evaluated through reliable behaviours that support the group's process and final work.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply criteria for evaluating production teamwork.

questions.prompt: A scene shifts from comedy to danger. Which lighting choice could support the change?
options: Move from bright even light to sharper contrast or lower intensity
Keep exactly the same light for every mood
Turn all lights off so actors cannot move safely
Add random flashing lights with no purpose
questions.correctAnswer: Move from bright even light to sharper contrast or lower intensity
questions.explanation: Lighting changes can guide the audience's emotional reading while maintaining safety and visibility.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply lighting choices to support mood shifts.

questions.prompt: A director wants actors to discover natural dialogue for a scripted scene. Which rehearsal activity best supports this?
options: Improvising the situation in their own words before returning to the script
Reading only stage directions without interaction
Memorising lines without understanding relationships
Skipping rehearsal until the final performance
questions.correctAnswer: Improvising the situation in their own words before returning to the script
questions.explanation: Improvisation can help actors understand objectives and relationships before refining scripted dialogue.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply improvisation to deepen scripted performance.

questions.prompt: A filmmaker needs to show two characters looking at each other across a table. Which rule helps preserve screen direction?
options: Keep the camera on one side of the imaginary action line unless the crossing is motivated
Place the camera randomly for every shot
Reverse eyelines without planning
Film only the table and not the characters
questions.correctAnswer: Keep the camera on one side of the imaginary action line unless the crossing is motivated
questions.explanation: The 180-degree guideline helps viewers understand where characters are in relation to each other.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply screen direction principles in dialogue scenes.

questions.prompt: A class is planning a public performance in the school hall. Which pre-performance checklist is most complete?
options: Script ready, rehearsed cues, safe set, tested sound, checked props, informed audience, and emergency plan
Only snacks and colourful posters
Only actor costumes with no technical check
Only a title and a prayer item
questions.correctAnswer: Script ready, rehearsed cues, safe set, tested sound, checked props, informed audience, and emergency plan
questions.explanation: Performance readiness combines artistic preparation, technical reliability, audience communication, and safety planning.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply readiness checks before public presentation.

questions.prompt: A performance has beautiful costumes, but the audience cannot understand the story. What is the strongest critique?
options: Design has not been integrated with clear dramatic action and communication
Costumes are the only element that matters in theatre
Audience understanding is never part of performance quality
The actors should ignore plot and focus on fabric
questions.correctAnswer: Design has not been integrated with clear dramatic action and communication
questions.explanation: Production elements should support the story, theme, and performance rather than replace them.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how production elements support dramatic communication.

questions.prompt: A short film uses handheld camera movement during a calm interview, making viewers distracted. What is the best analysis?
options: The camera style conflicts with the interview's intended tone and clarity
Handheld movement is always the most professional choice
The interview needs less understandable sound
The subject should move faster to match the camera
questions.correctAnswer: The camera style conflicts with the interview's intended tone and clarity
questions.explanation: Camera movement should serve meaning; unnecessary movement can distract from speech and subject presence.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse whether camera style supports scene purpose.

questions.prompt: A script begins with a strong conflict, but every later scene repeats the same argument with no new information. What is the main weakness?
options: The plot lacks escalation, discovery, and changing stakes
The script has too many turning points
The characters change too much too quickly
The ending is over-resolved from the start
questions.correctAnswer: The plot lacks escalation, discovery, and changing stakes
questions.explanation: Drama develops when pressure, choices, information, and consequences change from scene to scene.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse progression and escalation in dramatic writing.

questions.prompt: A director blocks all powerful characters on high levels and all powerless characters seated for an entire play. What is the likely issue?
options: The symbolism may become too fixed and predictable without changes or nuance
The staging has too much physical variety
Levels cannot communicate status in theatre
Every play must use only standing positions
questions.correctAnswer: The symbolism may become too fixed and predictable without changes or nuance
questions.explanation: Levels can show status, but strong staging also allows shifts, reversals, and complexity.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the effectiveness of symbolic blocking choices.

questions.prompt: A documentary includes interviews from only one side of a disputed community issue. What is the strongest ethical concern?
options: The film may misrepresent the issue by excluding relevant perspectives
The film automatically becomes more balanced
The camera angle is the only ethical factor
One interview is always enough for every topic
questions.correctAnswer: The film may misrepresent the issue by excluding relevant perspectives
questions.explanation: Responsible documentary practice considers fairness, context, consent, and representation of affected voices.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse fairness and representation in documentary production.

questions.prompt: A scene about reconciliation ends with both characters apologising immediately after a major betrayal. What should a reviewer question?
options: Whether the emotional shift is motivated by enough dramatic action
Whether all dialogue should be removed from the scene
Whether reconciliation can ever appear in drama
Whether costumes are more important than character change
questions.correctAnswer: Whether the emotional shift is motivated by enough dramatic action
questions.explanation: Character change is convincing when choices, discoveries, or consequences make the shift believable.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse motivation behind character change.

questions.prompt: A school film has clear images but speech is frequently covered by music. Which judgement is most accurate?
options: The sound mix weakens communication because dialogue should remain intelligible when it carries story
The music should always dominate every sound layer
Clear images make sound quality irrelevant
Dialogue becomes stronger when viewers cannot hear it
questions.correctAnswer: The sound mix weakens communication because dialogue should remain intelligible when it carries story
questions.explanation: Sound balance should support storytelling by prioritising the most important audio at each moment.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how sound balance affects film communication.

questions.prompt: A stage production uses borrowed community songs but does not acknowledge the source community. What is the strongest critique?
options: The production lacks ethical attribution and may disrespect cultural ownership
Borrowed material never needs acknowledgement
Audience entertainment cancels source responsibilities
Community songs cannot be part of performance
questions.correctAnswer: The production lacks ethical attribution and may disrespect cultural ownership
questions.explanation: Cultural material should be used with respect, permission where needed, and acknowledgement of its source.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate ethical use of cultural material in performance.

questions.prompt: An actor speaks loudly enough, but the performance feels flat because every line has the same stress and pace. What is the main acting issue?
options: Limited vocal modulation and unclear thought changes
Poor costume storage
Strong emotional variety
Accurate screen direction
questions.correctAnswer: Limited vocal modulation and unclear thought changes
questions.explanation: Effective vocal delivery varies stress, pace, pause, pitch, and tone according to intention and meaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse vocal choices in acting performance.

questions.prompt: A film sequence cuts from a joyful wedding dance to an empty room with wilted flowers. What does this contrast most likely create?
options: A shift in mood that suggests loss, memory, or changed circumstances
A technical error with no possible meaning
Proof that the scenes must be unrelated
A guarantee that the film is a comedy
questions.correctAnswer: A shift in mood that suggests loss, memory, or changed circumstances
questions.explanation: Juxtaposition can create meaning by placing contrasting images next to each other.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse meaning created through edited image contrast.

questions.prompt: A production spends most of its budget on social media adverts but has unsafe set pieces and no transport plan. What is the best evaluation?
options: The budget prioritises publicity over essential safety and production logistics
Marketing should always consume all funds
Unsafe set pieces are acceptable if the poster is attractive
Transport planning has no link to performance readiness
questions.correctAnswer: The budget prioritises publicity over essential safety and production logistics
questions.explanation: Budget evaluation should balance audience outreach with practical, safe, and reliable production needs.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate whether a production budget supports priorities and safety.

questions.prompt: A devised play includes many strong images, but no character has a clear want. What weakness should the group address?
options: The images need to connect to objectives, obstacles, and choices
The play has too much narrative clarity
Characters should never want anything in drama
All visual images should be removed immediately
questions.correctAnswer: The images need to connect to objectives, obstacles, and choices
questions.explanation: Powerful images become more dramatic when linked to character intention and action.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the link between image, objective, and dramatic action.

questions.prompt: A director asks actors to perform a traditional story with exaggerated accents for comedy. What is the key ethical risk?
options: The choice may stereotype or mock a community instead of representing it respectfully
Exaggeration always makes cultural work more accurate
Comedy removes all responsibility to audiences
Traditional stories cannot include humour
questions.correctAnswer: The choice may stereotype or mock a community instead of representing it respectfully
questions.explanation: Cultural representation should avoid mockery, harmful stereotypes, and careless distortion of identity.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse ethical risks in cultural representation.

questions.prompt: A film uses a close-up of a clenched fist before a character speaks calmly. What should an analyst consider first?
options: The image may reveal tension or subtext that contrasts with the spoken words
The close-up proves the character feels nothing
The shot has no relationship to performance
The dialogue must be deleted
questions.correctAnswer: The image may reveal tension or subtext that contrasts with the spoken words
questions.explanation: Film can reveal hidden emotion through visual details even when dialogue suggests control.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how visual detail communicates subtext.

questions.prompt: A theatre review says the chorus movements were energetic but distracted from the main speaker. What is the strongest interpretation?
options: Ensemble movement lacked focus control and did not support the central action
Energy always improves every stage moment
The main speaker should leave the stage
Chorus movement cannot be used in theatre
questions.correctAnswer: Ensemble movement lacked focus control and did not support the central action
questions.explanation: Ensemble work should direct attention intentionally rather than compete with important action.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse focus control in ensemble staging.

questions.prompt: A learner's adaptation changes a folktale so much that its moral lesson disappears. What should be evaluated?
options: Whether transformation has preserved the source's core meaning and purpose
Whether every adaptation must copy the source word for word
Whether moral lessons are forbidden in modern performance
Whether costumes are more important than story meaning
questions.correctAnswer: Whether transformation has preserved the source's core meaning and purpose
questions.explanation: Adaptation can update context, but it should make deliberate choices about what meaning remains central.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate fidelity and transformation in adaptation.

questions.prompt: A lighting plan uses a single bright wash for a play moving through dawn, afternoon, and night. What is the main limitation?
options: It fails to support time changes, mood shifts, and visual focus
It has too many varied lighting states
It makes the script impossible to perform
It proves lighting cannot tell time
questions.correctAnswer: It fails to support time changes, mood shifts, and visual focus
questions.explanation: Lighting should help communicate time, place, focus, and atmosphere where the production needs them.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse whether lighting design supports dramatic context.

questions.prompt: A performance about water conservation gives facts clearly but has no characters, conflict, or stakes. What is the strongest artistic weakness?
options: The issue has not been transformed into dramatic action
The performance contains too much character conflict
The facts should never appear in theatre
The audience will understand less if characters are added
questions.correctAnswer: The issue has not been transformed into dramatic action
questions.explanation: Educational theatre becomes more engaging when information is embodied through human choices and consequences.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how social issues can become dramatic action.

questions.prompt: A film group receives feedback that the ending feels unclear. Which evidence would best support that critique?
options: Viewers cannot identify what changed for the main character or issue
The final shot uses natural light
The credits are short
The film was recorded at school
questions.correctAnswer: Viewers cannot identify what changed for the main character or issue
questions.explanation: An ending should help viewers understand the outcome, shift, question, or consequence created by the story.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse audience understanding of narrative resolution.

questions.prompt: A rehearsal process lets one confident learner make every decision while others stay silent. What production risk is most likely?
options: Weak collaboration, reduced ownership, and missed creative ideas from the ensemble
Perfect democratic teamwork
Improved safety because fewer people speak
Automatic artistic excellence
questions.correctAnswer: Weak collaboration, reduced ownership, and missed creative ideas from the ensemble
questions.explanation: Collaborative production benefits from clear leadership, shared contribution, listening, and respect.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate leadership and participation in group production.

questions.prompt: A class must create a five-minute film about restoring trust after a broken promise. Which concept is strongest?
options: Two friends disagree after one leaks a secret, then repair trust through accountability and changed behaviour
A learner announces that trust is important and the film ends
Five unrelated shots of school buildings appear in random order
Characters forgive instantly before any conflict is shown
questions.correctAnswer: Two friends disagree after one leaks a secret, then repair trust through accountability and changed behaviour
questions.explanation: A strong concept gives characters, conflict, consequence, and a dramatic path toward change.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a focused screen concept from a value-based theme.

questions.prompt: A group is designing a theatre performance for a mixed-age community audience on road safety. Which plan is strongest?
options: Use a clear story, relatable characters, safe humour, practical choices, and respectful audience interaction
Use technical traffic-law terms only and no action
Show dangerous stunts to prove the point
Mock people who have made road mistakes
questions.correctAnswer: Use a clear story, relatable characters, safe humour, practical choices, and respectful audience interaction
questions.explanation: Community performance should be accessible, safe, respectful, and dramatically engaging.
questions.learningOutcome: Design audience-appropriate theatre for a community issue.

questions.prompt: A learner needs a rubric for assessing a Grade 11 short film project. Which criteria are most balanced?
options: Story clarity, shot choice, sound quality, editing, teamwork, ethics, audience impact, and reflection
Only camera price and costume colour
Only number of actors and length of credits
Only whether the film is funny
questions.correctAnswer: Story clarity, shot choice, sound quality, editing, teamwork, ethics, audience impact, and reflection
questions.explanation: A balanced rubric assesses both product and process across creative, technical, ethical, and reflective dimensions.
questions.learningOutcome: Create criteria for evaluating short film production.

questions.prompt: A theatre group has twelve performers and only four named characters. Which plan best uses the whole ensemble meaningfully?
options: Create chorus, soundscape, movement, crowd, memory, and transition roles that support the central action
Leave eight performers backstage without tasks
Give every performer identical lines in every scene
Remove named characters so all roles are the same
questions.correctAnswer: Create chorus, soundscape, movement, crowd, memory, and transition roles that support the central action
questions.explanation: Ensemble design can distribute performance responsibility while strengthening story, rhythm, and stage images.
questions.learningOutcome: Design ensemble roles that serve a production concept.

questions.prompt: A team must choose between a realistic courtroom set and a symbolic set of benches, files, and shadows. Which criterion should guide the decision?
options: Which design best supports theme, budget, safety, visibility, scene changes, and audience understanding
Which design uses the most objects regardless of meaning
Which option is hardest to carry into the hall
Which set lets actors avoid rehearsing
questions.correctAnswer: Which design best supports theme, budget, safety, visibility, scene changes, and audience understanding
questions.explanation: Design choices should balance artistic meaning with practical constraints and audience clarity.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate and select design approaches for a production concept.

questions.prompt: A film crew wants to produce a documentary using stories from local artisans. Which workflow is most ethical?
options: Seek informed consent, explain purpose, credit contributors, represent context fairly, and store footage securely
Record secretly because public places have no ethics
Edit statements to create false conflict
Publish personal details without permission
questions.correctAnswer: Seek informed consent, explain purpose, credit contributors, represent context fairly, and store footage securely
questions.explanation: Ethical documentary work protects participants and respects the truthfulness and context of their stories.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate ethical workflow for community-based documentary work.

questions.prompt: A five-shot sequence must show a learner deciding to report exam cheating without dialogue. Which sequence is clearest?
options: Sees cheating, hesitates, notices unfair marks, grips report form, walks to teacher's office
Shows a tree, a gate, a shoe, a blank wall, and a sunset
Starts with the teacher praising honesty before any problem appears
Repeats the same close-up of a pen five times
questions.correctAnswer: Sees cheating, hesitates, notices unfair marks, grips report form, walks to teacher's office
questions.explanation: A coherent visual sequence shows observation, inner conflict, reason, decision, and action.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a shot sequence that communicates ethical decision-making.

questions.prompt: A devised play about youth unemployment risks becoming a lecture. Which creative strategy best makes it dramatic?
options: Build scenes around characters pursuing work, facing barriers, making choices, and discovering alternatives
Have actors recite employment statistics only
Remove all conflict so the message is polite
Use posters instead of performance action
questions.correctAnswer: Build scenes around characters pursuing work, facing barriers, making choices, and discovering alternatives
questions.explanation: A social theme becomes dramatic when ideas are carried by character objectives, obstacles, choices, and consequences.
questions.learningOutcome: Create dramatic action from a contemporary social issue.

questions.prompt: A group is preparing a director's concept note for a stage adaptation of a Kenyan oral story. Which content is most complete?
options: Source, theme, audience, performance style, ethical permissions, design approach, casting plan, and intended impact
Only the title and actor names
Only a list of props with no source or theme
Only the final ticket price
questions.correctAnswer: Source, theme, audience, performance style, ethical permissions, design approach, casting plan, and intended impact
questions.explanation: A concept note should explain the artistic, practical, ethical, and audience-facing choices guiding production.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a director's concept note for adapted performance.

questions.prompt: A final Grade 11 Performing Arts portfolio should show both process and product. Which evidence set is strongest?
options: Research notes, script drafts, rehearsal logs, design plans, consent records, performance evidence, feedback, and reflection
Only the finished poster
Only informal messages between friends
Only a list of favourite films
questions.correctAnswer: Research notes, script drafts, rehearsal logs, design plans, consent records, performance evidence, feedback, and reflection
questions.explanation: A strong portfolio documents creative development, ethical practice, collaboration, final work, and learning from feedback.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a portfolio that documents Performing Arts process and achievement.
